card.title: We Learned to Win Together
card.instruction: Treat your memories of competing side by side as proof that you still understand one another better than anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're giving me our old quiz-final look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're on different teams. I'm not asking for answers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Left eyebrow means you have two answers and hate both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My captain thinks I've got something in my eye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She hasn't sat through your geography rounds. I'll ask for another minute; you found Madagascar in the last one.

mechanism: A uses former shared quiz pressure to claim privileged understanding of B despite separate teams.
confusable: Unlike cheating or nostalgia, A must interpret B through the history rather than supply an answer.
comparison: S199-b requests time based on an old geography recovery; S199-a identifies readiness despite a daughter's worry.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
